articles.title: Kerala HC allows hotel Radisson Blu in Kochi to operate till 3 a.m.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala High Court has allowed hotel Radisson Blu, Kochi, to operate till 3 a.m.
Justice Murali Purushothaman set aside a notice by police authorities banning the hotel from operating and conducting DJ parties after 11 p.m.

K. Mahadevan, the hotel's licensee, had challenged the notice issued by the police, alleging that the hotel had obtained the right to extended operation after meeting all the required criteria, including payment of additional licence fees.
The State had contended that allowing the hotel to operate and conduct DJ parties till 3 a.m. would cause disruptions to public order and act as a venue for drug-related transactions.

However, the court held that the police could not curtail or restrict the operating hours of the hotel, unless the State government issued regulations curtailing the operating hours. Mere possibility of criminal activities could not justify imposing restrictions under the Kerala Police Act on the extended operating hours of an FL3 hotel permitted under the Foreign Liquor Amendment Rules, the court stated.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mere possibility of criminal activities could not justify imposing restrictions under the Kerala Police Act on the extended operating hours of an FL3 hotel permitted under the Foreign Liquor Amendment Rules, the court stated.

articles.title: Tasmac’s liquor sales in Tamil Nadu touch ₹441 crore this Deepavali amid POS machine glitches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) has recorded liquor sales worth ₹441.38 crore during Deepavali 2026. According to sources, on the eve of Deepavali, Tasmac sold liquor worth over ₹234.75 crore and on the day of the festival the sales stood at ₹206.63 crore.

Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore. Salem reported sales of ₹87.52 crore and Coimbatore at ₹70.66 crore. As Monday was a holiday, liquor sales are expected to remain at similar levels (sales of approximately ₹192 crore are expected).

Those tracking the liquor market in Tamil Nadu say sales have dipped marginally this year (Tasmac does not officially disclose its Deepavali sales figures. The data has been collated from various sources for several years).

While some salesmen attributed the dip in sales to machines getting stuck and confusion surrounding the buy back scheme, others said that liquor sales had been unusually high over the past week, with crowds slightly larger than usual. “People were worried that shops might not open because of the issues surrounding the buy back scheme. So, many started stocking up for the festival as early as last week,” said a salesman at a shop in the T. Nagar region.

A senior Tasmac official said that the issues with POS machines would be resolved soon and that around 1,000 new POS machines would be deployed across outlets soon. “Wherever there is a requirement we will deploy these machines.” the official added.
When asked about the issues with POS machines, Minister for Prohibition and Excise K. Vignesh questioned: “The POS machines were working until November 1. What happened after that?”

He also said that around 44 salesmen had been suspended between November 1 and 5 for violating MRP norms. “We have received more complaints of similar violations and will initiate action on them as well,” he added.

Tasmac sources said the corporation is estimated to have collected around ₹38 crore through the Environment Protection Cess. From November 1, 2026, a ₹10 Environmental and Social Welfare Cess was levied on liquor sales to facilitate the buy back of empty bottles. The cess was included in the MRP.

As on July 2026, Tasmac has 4,048 retail vending shops and a workforce of 22,877 (6,473 supervisors, 14,379 salespersons, and 2,025 assistant salespersons). For the year 2025-2026, Tasmac earned a revenue of ₹50,845 crore.

articles.title: Cyclones Arnab and Murasu damaged crops on 4.61 lakh hectares in Andhra, say officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu has directed officials to expedite the enumeration of crop losses caused by Cyclones Arnab and Murasu and ensure that no eligible farmer is left out of the assessment.

Reviewing the damage with senior officials of the Agriculture and Horticulture departments through a teleconference on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the Minister was informed that the two cyclones had damaged agricultural crops on 4,61,194 hectares and horticultural crops on 29,960 hectares.

According to officials, Cyclone Arnab affected 3,27,843 hectares, or 30.05% of the total cultivated area of 10,90,933 hectares across 15 districts. As many as 5,23,136 farmers were affected, while the estimated production loss stood at 9,78,091 tonnes, involving a financial loss of ₹2,392.84 crore.

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district suffered extensive damage, with 99.19% of its cultivated area affected. The estimated financial loss there was ₹348.88 crore, affecting 94,808 farmers. The relief requirement was estimated at ₹815.57 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and ₹714.96 crore under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).

Cyclone Murasu damaged crops on 1,33,351 hectares, accounting for 23.71% of the total cultivated area of 5,62,445 hectares across nine districts. The disaster affected 1,86,269 farmers, with an estimated production loss of 3,38,302 tonnes and a financial loss of ₹816.53 crore. The estimated relief requirement was ₹321.64 crore under the SDRF and ₹266.67 crore under the NDRF.

The horticultural sector also suffered extensive damage. Cyclone Arnab affected 23,211.48 hectares in 1,310 villages across 215 mandals in 15 districts, impacting 58,990 farmers. Enumeration had been completed for 23,035.08 hectares, covering 58,630 farmers, accounting for 99.24% of the affected area. Registration of another 176.40 hectares involving 360 farmers was pending. Fourteen districts had completed the exercise, while Krishna district had recorded 86.67% progress.

Cyclone Murasu damaged 6,748.52 hectares of horticultural crops in 530 villages across 106 mandals in eight districts, affecting 12,586 farmers. However, enumeration had been completed for only 2,211.73 hectares, covering 3,392 farmers, or 32.77% of the affected area. Registration of the remaining 4,536.79 hectares involving 9,194 farmers was pending.

Mr. Atchannaidu instructed officials to conduct a comprehensive field-level assessment of the damage caused by both cyclones and identify the unrecorded crop area and affected farmers district-wise. He asked them to complete the enumeration expeditiously and ensure that every eligible farmer was covered.

articles.title: PM Modi and Railway Minister likely to flag off Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Goa Vande Bharat Express on November 13
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw are likely to flag off the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express on November 13 from Bengaluru and Mangaluru Junction simultaneously.

Mr. Modi will be in Bengaluru to dedicate the 7.5 km Namma Metro Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere along the Bannerghatta Road, as announced earlier by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. During this occasion, the Prime Minister will also remotely flag off the Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express starting from Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, sources in the South Western Railway (SWR) told The Hindu .

Mr. Vaishnaw, as promised to Members of Parliament from the coast, would launch the new service from Mangaluru Junction at around 2.30 p.m., sources said. Both the down and up inaugural specials would run simultaneously towards Bengaluru and Mangaluru. Regular services of the VB Express could start within a day or two, sources said adding regular services would operate out of Yeshwantpur; and not SMVTB.

The Railway Minister had, on September 29, announced that the Ministry would introduce Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express as Train No. 26655/656 by extending the existing Mangaluru Central-Madgaon-Mangaluru Central VB Express (Train No. 20646/645). Releasing the timetable of the extended service on October 30, the Ministry had said the services would start at an early convenient date or ‘no booking’ date for Mangaluru-Madgaon-Mangaluru VB.

The Bengaluru-Madgaon VB Express would have 12 halts, excluding the originating and terminating stations. They are, Shravanabelagola, Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Kabaka Puttur, Mangaluru Junction, Udupi, Kundapura, Byndoor, Murdeshwar, Gokarna Road and Karwar.

While the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon service leaves Yeshwantpur at 7.35 a.m. to reach Madgaon at 8.55 p.m. taking 12.20 hours except on Wednesdays, the Madgaon-Yeshwantpur service departs Madgaon at 8.20 a.m. to reach Yeshwantpur at 9.15 p.m. taking 13 hours except on Thursdays.
Two rakes required for the service are kept ready, sources added.

articles.title: HMWS&SB fines Akshayakalpa Farms ₹20,000 for wasting drinking water in Hyderabad’s Jubilee Hills
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has imposed a fine of ₹20,000 on Akshayakalpa Farms and Foods Private Limited in Jubilee Hills for using drinking water to clean floors. The Board has also temporarily disconnected the sewage connection at the premises as part of its drive to curb the wastage and misuse of drinking water.

The action was taken after officials found drinking water being used for floor cleaning at the company’s premises in Journalist Colony, Road No. 70, Jubilee Hills. HMWS&SB said it had intensified inspections across Hyderabad in anticipation of potential water availability challenges during the upcoming summer and was taking measures to conserve drinking water.

Officials have urged residents and commercial establishments to restrict the use of drinking water to essential purposes such as drinking and cooking. They have cautioned against using potable water for floor cleaning, vehicle washing, gardening and construction activities, and advised the public to use treated water supplied from sewage treatment plants (STPs) for such purposes.

The Board warned that inspections would continue across the city and strict action would be taken against establishments found wasting or misusing drinking water. It has also appealed to citizens to report instances of drinking water wastage by sending details, photographs or videos to its WhatsApp number 99499 30003.

articles.title: NCW receives 1.5 lakh complaints annually, domestic violence tops list: Vijaya Rahatkar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Commission for Women receives around 1.5 lakh complaints annually, with domestic violence accounting for the highest number of cases, NCW Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has said.

In an interview with PTI , Ms. Rahatkar said there are multiple ways, including the commission's online portal, Management Information System (MIS), email, in person and its 24x7 helpline, for women to approach the NCW to register their complaints.
"We receive around 1.5 lakh complaints annually. If we look at the cases falling under our mandate, domestic violence accounts for the highest number of complaints," she said.
"No woman should feel that she could not approach the NCW simply because she did not know how to file a complaint," she said, referring to the commission's helpline number 14490 and its website.

Ms. Rahatkar also highlighted the commission's outreach initiative, 'Rashtriya Mahila Aayog Aapke Dwar', under which it conducts public hearings in different states to reach women who may find it difficult to approach the NCW.
"We decided that if these women cannot come to us, we will go to them," she said.

She said that since she took charge as NCW Chairperson, the commission has conducted more than 200 in-person public hearings in villages and other locations across the country over the past 1.5 years.

"We have met a large number of women and tried to resolve their problems," she said, adding that the NCW also conducts programmes to create awareness about women's legal rights and build their confidence.
Ms. Rahatkar said the NCW should be seen as "maayka" (maternal home) by women.

"I have always told women and daughters across the country that the National Commission for Women should feel like their maayka -- their maternal home. There should be no fear or hesitation in approaching the commission," she said.

"When a woman faces a problem, whom does she approach first? She goes to her mother. Similarly, the commission should be like a maternal home for women. They can approach us without fear or hesitation," she added.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ⁠Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s ‌approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”

Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: the hurdles, the risks and the politics | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport and a national identity card from the Government of Bangladesh on Monday (November 9, 2026). In response, Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said that Bangladesh seeks her extradition under an “acceptable prisoner transfer process”. This is the latest episode in the Hasina saga that began when she came to India on August 5, 2024, after the student-people uprising toppled her government.

Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it. How to return to face justice and yet emerge as a leader of her country is the big challenge before her. She has refused to apologise for the crackdown, saying the police did not take her orders but responded to angry agitators and militants who had provoked them.

articles.title: U.S.-brokered talks are set to start in Abu Dhabi to discuss Ukraine-Russia peace deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States start on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) in the United Arab Emirates, renewing a push for peace after several rounds of negotiations earlier this year.

The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees. U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a "negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment.”
Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal to end the full-scale war, now nearing its five-year mark .

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.

Mr. Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Mr. Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia has not been able to take on the battlefield. Mr. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.

Russia's chief negotiator is Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who has led Moscow's team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul, Turkey, in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff's operational department Yuri Zhigarlovsky.

Ukraine's delegation is led by Rustem Umerov, head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service, who also attended earlier talks. It also reportedly includes Mr. Zelenskyy's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Mr. Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.

articles.title: G7 attention in Paris turns to Ukraine while U.S.-mediated talks get underway in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his counterparts from the Group of 7 developed democracies are turning their attention toward Ukraine and how to support it in its struggle to defend itself from Russia. As three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States get underway in the United Arab Emirates, top G7 diplomats are meeting on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with Ukraine's foreign minister in France.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha will start his day in Paris in talks with Mr. Rubio before heading to the French Foreign Ministry for a larger group meeting with the entire G7. They will discuss defense and security assistance to Ukraine, which President Donald Trump's administration has reduced, causing consternation not only in Kyiv but in capitals across Europe, the largest of which — Paris, Berlin, Rome and London — are G7 members.
It was not immediately clear if the U.S. or any of its G7 partners would announce any new assistance for Ukraine.

Meanwhile, in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will be meeting Russian and Ukrainian officials in part to persuade Moscow to agree to broader negotiations that would include key European officials on how to end nearly five years of war.

In Paris, Europeans have been clamouring for a seat at the table in Abu Dhabi, but two US officials said Monday that representatives from Britain, Germany, France, NATO and the European Union would not join the main talks but rather discuss potential security guarantees and the long-term security architecture between Russia and Europe beforehand.

Russia has resisted European participation in negotiations and insisted the talks should proceed strictly as a trilateral format involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The three last held talks in February.
But on Monday (November 9) in Paris, German Foreign Minister Johan Wadephul, who met separately with Rubio on the sidelines of the G7, was emphatic that Europe must be included.

“I am still very grateful to the United States of America for making every effort to get the parties to the conflict to the table,” he said. “But I made clear again here that Europe belongs at this table. There can be no solution without Europe, only with Europe.”
Mr. Rubio said the U.S. has no objection to eventual European involvement in the direct talks, but that it wasn't yet time.

“Ultimately, it would be a positive, but we've got a ways to go,” he told reporters after a full day of group and bilateral meetings with G7 counterparts. “But, no, it's good that they're talking, it's good that the trilateral talks are on again. It's better than not having talks.”
On the eve of the talks, Russia battered Ukraine's power grid again on Monday (November 9), and Ukrainian forces hit another of Russia's biggest oil refineries.

The two countries remain locked in battle with no sign that either side is ready to budge from their demands. The war has already killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians, analysts and humanitarian organizations say.

articles.title: UFC chief Dana White declines Donald Trump's White House job offer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Mr. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday (November 7) that he had asked Mr. White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding."
The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday (November 9), and Mr. Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.
"So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Mr. Trump said.
"Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," Mr. White replied.
Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody."

The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Mr. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" Mr. White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat.
Mr. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.
But there was also some scepticism about the president's announcement, and Mr. Trump said Sunday (November 8) night that he had been joking.
Leading out Mr. White to the podium on Monday (November 9), Mr. Trump said he had been "having a little fun."
"He's a great guy," Mr. Trump told the room full of reporters. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you."

articles.title: Bill in U.S. Congress to recognise Deepavali as federal holiday, 19 lawmakers back proposal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A group of U.S. lawmakers, led by Grace Meng, on Monday (November 9, 2026) said they will re-introduce a bill in the House of Representatives to recognise Deepavali as a federal holiday.

Ms. Meng, the chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), and 19 U.S. lawmakers, including Raja Krishnamoorthi, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Ro Khanna and Ami Bera, re-introduced the Deepavali Day Act to recognise the festival as a federal holiday.

“My Diwali Day Act will help educate Americans about the importance of this day, and I will continue working to create a more inclusive nation that honours the rich cultural traditions of its people,” Ms. Meng said in a statement.

The draft legislation describes Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, as one of the most important holidays of the year for many religious groups including Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists as well as billions in the South Asian, Southeast Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities.

Ms. Meng said while the celebration holds a different significance for these diverse religious, ethnic and cultural groups, the Festival of Lights unites those who observe with reflection, prayer and gathering with loved ones.

“Diwali represents the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognising Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, are valued members of our society,” Ms. Meng said.
Hindu and South Asian communities across the country are facing an alarming rise in hate, intimidation, and targeted violence, a CAPAC statement said.

“This includes vandalism at Hindu places of worship, an attempted mass shooting during Navratri festivities at a Hindu temple in Illinois, and the recent racist disruption of a Diwali celebration in Washington State. CAPAC has been sounding the alarm that these acts of hate must be taken seriously and investigated by federal authorities,” it said.
If the Bill is passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the 12th federally recognised holiday in the United States.
Establishing a federal holiday for Deepavali, and the day off it would provide, would demonstrate that the government values the rich cultures and traditions of its citizens.
Ms. Meng is also the author of the Lunar New Year Day Act, which would establish Lunar New Year as a federally recognised holiday.

The Bill is also endorsed by Asian Americans Advancing Justice (AAJC), Asian American Federation (AAF), Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA), Hindus for Human Rights, Hindu Temple Society of North America, Indian American Impact, Indian Diaspora Council, Indo-Caribbean Alliance, International Commission on Dalit Rights, National Asian Pacific American Bar Association (NAPABA), National Council of Asian Pacific Americans (NCAPA), OCA-Asian Pacific American Advocates, Sikh American Legal Defense and Education Fund (SALDEF), The Sikh Cultural Society, The Sikh Coalition, South Asian Impact Foundation, and Southeast Asia Resource Action Center (SEARAC).

fullParagraphs: In September 2026, China’s government unveiled an ambitious 10-year plan to reform its universities. Driving the change is an increasingly challenging job market for the country’s close to 13 million college graduates, who are facing the twin disruptions of AI and a slowing economy. Under the plan, dozens of graduate programmes are being disbanded, while universities themselves will be categorised and tasked with either pursuing research, applications or skills development.

A combination of factors, some not too dissimilar to the current challenges in India’s own job market, has left policymakers grappling with a tepid job market and a vast number of graduates facing dim job prospects. Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

articles.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.
The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions.
Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).
These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence.
ChatGPT's 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further.
With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies.
Washington bans the export of Nvidia's top-end "Blackwell" and "Rubin" GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications.
The policy also allows the United States's top AI labs to maintain their global lead.
Huang has lobbied the U.S. government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives.
This year, Washington eased controls on Nvidia's previously banned -- and less powerful -- "H200" chip, with the United States taking a 25% cut of sales.
But U.S. conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum.
Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on U.S. rivals.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

The church sees the initiative as more than a fitness facility. “We want to groom a healthy generation. Many people suffer from lifestyle diseases, while youngsters often turn to private fitness centres. We felt that providing basic facilities here would benefit the community. Spirituality is also about nurturing a healthy mind and body. We consider this a form of spiritual service,” says assistant vicar Fr. Jees Akkara.

For Fr. Eluvathingal, there is another purpose. “Youngsters rarely come to church or participate in its activities these days. This is also an opportunity to bring more of them into the church community,” he says.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
• Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Kerala HC allows hotel Radisson Blu in Kochi to operate till 3 a.m.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala High Court has allowed hotel Radisson Blu, Kochi, to operate till 3 a.m.
Justice Murali Purushothaman set aside a notice by police authorities banning the hotel from operating and conducting DJ parties after 11 p.m.

K. Mahadevan, the hotel's licensee, had challenged the notice issued by the police, alleging that the hotel had obtained the right to extended operation after meeting all the required criteria, including payment of additional licence fees.
The State had contended that allowing the hotel to operate and conduct DJ parties till 3 a.m. would cause disruptions to public order and act as a venue for drug-related transactions.

However, the court held that the police could not curtail or restrict the operating hours of the hotel, unless the State government issued regulations curtailing the operating hours. Mere possibility of criminal activities could not justify imposing restrictions under the Kerala Police Act on the extended operating hours of an FL3 hotel permitted under the Foreign Liquor Amendment Rules, the court stated.

articles.title: Tasmac’s liquor sales in Tamil Nadu touch ₹441 crore this Deepavali amid POS machine glitches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) has recorded liquor sales worth ₹441.38 crore during Deepavali 2026. According to sources, on the eve of Deepavali, Tasmac sold liquor worth over ₹234.75 crore and on the day of the festival the sales stood at ₹206.63 crore.

Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore. Salem reported sales of ₹87.52 crore and Coimbatore at ₹70.66 crore. As Monday was a holiday, liquor sales are expected to remain at similar levels (sales of approximately ₹192 crore are expected).

Those tracking the liquor market in Tamil Nadu say sales have dipped marginally this year (Tasmac does not officially disclose its Deepavali sales figures. The data has been collated from various sources for several years).

While some salesmen attributed the dip in sales to machines getting stuck and confusion surrounding the buy back scheme, others said that liquor sales had been unusually high over the past week, with crowds slightly larger than usual. “People were worried that shops might not open because of the issues surrounding the buy back scheme. So, many started stocking up for the festival as early as last week,” said a salesman at a shop in the T. Nagar region.

A senior Tasmac official said that the issues with POS machines would be resolved soon and that around 1,000 new POS machines would be deployed across outlets soon. “Wherever there is a requirement we will deploy these machines.” the official added.
When asked about the issues with POS machines, Minister for Prohibition and Excise K. Vignesh questioned: “The POS machines were working until November 1. What happened after that?”

He also said that around 44 salesmen had been suspended between November 1 and 5 for violating MRP norms. “We have received more complaints of similar violations and will initiate action on them as well,” he added.

Tasmac sources said the corporation is estimated to have collected around ₹38 crore through the Environment Protection Cess. From November 1, 2026, a ₹10 Environmental and Social Welfare Cess was levied on liquor sales to facilitate the buy back of empty bottles. The cess was included in the MRP.

As on July 2026, Tasmac has 4,048 retail vending shops and a workforce of 22,877 (6,473 supervisors, 14,379 salespersons, and 2,025 assistant salespersons). For the year 2025-2026, Tasmac earned a revenue of ₹50,845 crore.

articles.title: Cyclones Arnab and Murasu damaged crops on 4.61 lakh hectares in Andhra, say officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu has directed officials to expedite the enumeration of crop losses caused by Cyclones Arnab and Murasu and ensure that no eligible farmer is left out of the assessment.

Reviewing the damage with senior officials of the Agriculture and Horticulture departments through a teleconference on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the Minister was informed that the two cyclones had damaged agricultural crops on 4,61,194 hectares and horticultural crops on 29,960 hectares.

According to officials, Cyclone Arnab affected 3,27,843 hectares, or 30.05% of the total cultivated area of 10,90,933 hectares across 15 districts. As many as 5,23,136 farmers were affected, while the estimated production loss stood at 9,78,091 tonnes, involving a financial loss of ₹2,392.84 crore.

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district suffered extensive damage, with 99.19% of its cultivated area affected. The estimated financial loss there was ₹348.88 crore, affecting 94,808 farmers. The relief requirement was estimated at ₹815.57 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and ₹714.96 crore under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).

Cyclone Murasu damaged crops on 1,33,351 hectares, accounting for 23.71% of the total cultivated area of 5,62,445 hectares across nine districts. The disaster affected 1,86,269 farmers, with an estimated production loss of 3,38,302 tonnes and a financial loss of ₹816.53 crore. The estimated relief requirement was ₹321.64 crore under the SDRF and ₹266.67 crore under the NDRF.

The horticultural sector also suffered extensive damage. Cyclone Arnab affected 23,211.48 hectares in 1,310 villages across 215 mandals in 15 districts, impacting 58,990 farmers. Enumeration had been completed for 23,035.08 hectares, covering 58,630 farmers, accounting for 99.24% of the affected area. Registration of another 176.40 hectares involving 360 farmers was pending. Fourteen districts had completed the exercise, while Krishna district had recorded 86.67% progress.

Cyclone Murasu damaged 6,748.52 hectares of horticultural crops in 530 villages across 106 mandals in eight districts, affecting 12,586 farmers. However, enumeration had been completed for only 2,211.73 hectares, covering 3,392 farmers, or 32.77% of the affected area. Registration of the remaining 4,536.79 hectares involving 9,194 farmers was pending.

Mr. Atchannaidu instructed officials to conduct a comprehensive field-level assessment of the damage caused by both cyclones and identify the unrecorded crop area and affected farmers district-wise. He asked them to complete the enumeration expeditiously and ensure that every eligible farmer was covered.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw are likely to flag off the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express on November 13 from Bengaluru and Mangaluru Junction simultaneously.

Mr. Modi will be in Bengaluru to dedicate the 7.5 km Namma Metro Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere along the Bannerghatta Road, as announced earlier by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, sources in the South Western Railway (SWR) told The Hindu .

Mr. Vaishnaw, as promised to Members of Parliament from the coast, would launch the new service from Mangaluru Junction at around 2.30 p.m., sources said. Both the down and up inaugural specials would run simultaneously towards Bengaluru and Mangaluru. Regular services of the VB Express could start within a day or two, sources said adding regular services would operate out of Yeshwantpur; and not SMVTB.

Releasing the timetable of the extended service on October 30, the Ministry had said the services would start at an early convenient date or ‘no booking’ date for Mangaluru-Madgaon-Mangaluru VB.

The Bengaluru-Madgaon VB Express would have 12 halts, excluding the originating and terminating stations. They are, Shravanabelagola, Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Kabaka Puttur, Mangaluru Junction, Udupi, Kundapura, Byndoor, Murdeshwar, Gokarna Road and Karwar.

While the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon service leaves Yeshwantpur at 7.35 a.m. to reach Madgaon at 8.55 p.m. taking 12.20 hours except on Wednesdays, the Madgaon-Yeshwantpur service departs Madgaon at 8.20 a.m. to reach Yeshwantpur at 9.15 p.m. taking 13 hours except on Thursdays.

articles.title: HMWS&SB fines Akshayakalpa Farms ₹20,000 for wasting drinking water in Hyderabad’s Jubilee Hills
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has imposed a fine of ₹20,000 on Akshayakalpa Farms and Foods Private Limited in Jubilee Hills for using drinking water to clean floors. The Board has also temporarily disconnected the sewage connection at the premises as part of its drive to curb the wastage and misuse of drinking water.

The action was taken after officials found drinking water being used for floor cleaning at the company’s premises in Journalist Colony, Road No. 70, Jubilee Hills. HMWS&SB said it had intensified inspections across Hyderabad in anticipation of potential water availability challenges during the upcoming summer and was taking measures to conserve drinking water.

Officials have urged residents and commercial establishments to restrict the use of drinking water to essential purposes such as drinking and cooking. They have cautioned against using potable water for floor cleaning, vehicle washing, gardening and construction activities, and advised the public to use treated water supplied from sewage treatment plants (STPs) for such purposes.

The Board warned that inspections would continue across the city and strict action would be taken against establishments found wasting or misusing drinking water. It has also appealed to citizens to report instances of drinking water wastage by sending details, photographs or videos to its WhatsApp number 99499 30003.

articles.title: NCW receives 1.5 lakh complaints annually, domestic violence tops list: Vijaya Rahatkar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Commission for Women receives around 1.5 lakh complaints annually, with domestic violence accounting for the highest number of cases, NCW Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has said.

In an interview with PTI , Ms. Rahatkar said there are multiple ways, including the commission's online portal, Management Information System (MIS), email, in person and its 24x7 helpline, for women to approach the NCW to register their complaints.
"We receive around 1.5 lakh complaints annually. If we look at the cases falling under our mandate, domestic violence accounts for the highest number of complaints," she said.
"No woman should feel that she could not approach the NCW simply because she did not know how to file a complaint," she said, referring to the commission's helpline number 14490 and its website.

Ms. Rahatkar also highlighted the commission's outreach initiative, 'Rashtriya Mahila Aayog Aapke Dwar', under which it conducts public hearings in different states to reach women who may find it difficult to approach the NCW.
"We decided that if these women cannot come to us, we will go to them," she said.

She said that since she took charge as NCW Chairperson, the commission has conducted more than 200 in-person public hearings in villages and other locations across the country over the past 1.5 years.

"We have met a large number of women and tried to resolve their problems," she said, adding that the NCW also conducts programmes to create awareness about women's legal rights and build their confidence.
Ms. Rahatkar said the NCW should be seen as "maayka" (maternal home) by women.

"I have always told women and daughters across the country that the National Commission for Women should feel like their maayka -- their maternal home. There should be no fear or hesitation in approaching the commission," she said.

"When a woman faces a problem, whom does she approach first? She goes to her mother. Similarly, the commission should be like a maternal home for women. They can approach us without fear or hesitation," she added.

fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: the hurdles, the risks and the politics | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport and a national identity card from the Government of Bangladesh on Monday (November 9, 2026). In response, Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said that Bangladesh seeks her extradition under an “acceptable prisoner transfer process”. This is the latest episode in the Hasina saga that began when she came to India on August 5, 2024, after the student-people uprising toppled her government.

Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it. How to return to face justice and yet emerge as a leader of her country is the big challenge before her. She has refused to apologise for the crackdown, saying the police did not take her orders but responded to angry agitators and militants who had provoked them.

articles.title: U.S.-brokered talks are set to start in Abu Dhabi to discuss Ukraine-Russia peace deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States start on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) in the United Arab Emirates, renewing a push for peace after several rounds of negotiations earlier this year.

The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees. U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a "negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment.”
Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal to end the full-scale war, now nearing its five-year mark .

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.

Mr. Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Mr. Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia has not been able to take on the battlefield. Mr. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.

Russia's chief negotiator is Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who has led Moscow's team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul, Turkey, in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff's operational department Yuri Zhigarlovsky.

Ukraine's delegation is led by Rustem Umerov, head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service, who also attended earlier talks. It also reportedly includes Mr. Zelenskyy's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Mr. Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.
